papers.title: Atomistic-Based Fatigue Property Normalization Through Maximum A Posteriori Optimization in Additive Manufacturing
papers.abstract: This work presents a multiscale, microstructure-aware framework for predicting fatigue strength distributions in additively manufactured (AM) alloys-specifically, laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) AlSi10Mg and Ti-6Al-4V-by integrating density functional theory (DFT), instrumented indentation, and Bayesian inference. The methodology leverages principles common to all 3D printing (additive manufacturing) processes: layer-wise material deposition, process-induced defect formation (such as porosity and residual stress), and microstructural tailoring through parameter control, which collectively differentiate AM from conventional manufacturing. By linking DFT-derived cohesive energies with indentation-based modulus measurements and a MAP-based statistical model, we quantify the effect of additive-manufactured microstructural heterogeneity on fatigue performance. Quantitative validation demonstrates that the predicted fatigue strength distributions agree with experimental high-cycle and very-high-cycle fatigue (HCF/VHCF) data, with posterior modes and 95 % credible intervals of σ^fAlSi10Mg=86-7+8MPa and σ^fTi-6Al-4V=115-9+10MPa, respectively. The resulting Woehler (S-N) curves and Paris crack-growth parameters envelop more than 92 % of the measured coupon data, confirming both accuracy and robustness. Furthermore, global sensitivity analysis reveals that volumetric porosity and residual stress account for over 70 % of the fatigue strength variance, highlighting the central role of process-structure relationships unique to AM. The presented framework thus provides a predictive, physically interpretable, and data-efficient pathway for microstructure-informed fatigue design in additively manufactured metals, and is readily extensible to other AM alloys and process variants.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文提出了一个集成密度泛函理论和贝叶斯推断的多尺度框架，用于预测增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的疲劳强度分布，并直接与实验数据验证。
llm.why_not_core: The paper also includes AlSi10Mg, but Ti-6Al-4V is explicitly treated and the framework is generalizable; it does not cover post-processing or femoral stem applications.

summary_zh.motivation: 增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的疲劳性能受微观结构异质性影响，需要预测性框架。
summary_zh.method: 结合密度泛函理论、仪器化压痕和最大后验概率统计模型的多尺度方法。
summary_zh.result: 预测的疲劳强度分布与实验高周和极高周疲劳数据吻合，孔隙率和残余应力解释超过70%的方差。
summary_zh.validation: 用实验HCF/VHCF数据验证，Wöhler曲线和Paris参数覆盖92%以上的实测数据。

summary_en.motivation: To address the challenge of predicting fatigue strength in additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V by accounting for microstructural heterogeneity.
summary_en.method: A multiscale framework integrating density functional theory, instrumented indentation, and maximum a posteriori Bayesian optimization to derive fatigue strength distributions.
summary_en.result: Predicted fatigue strengths (115 MPa for Ti-6Al-4V) with 95% credible intervals match experimental data, and sensitivity analysis attributes over 70% of variance to porosity and residual stress.
summary_en.validation: Validated against experimental high-cycle and very-high-cycle fatigue data, with Wöhler curves and Paris crack-growth parameters enveloping more than 92% of coupon measurements.

papers.title: Mechanical property and wear behavior of graphene-reinforced Ti-6Al-4V prepared by vacuum arc melting
papers.abstract: • Novel Fabrication Method: A method of pre-homogenizing the materials before vacuum arc melting was developed to fabricate FLG/SiC/Ti-6Al-4V (TC4) composites, enabling the production of dense materials with enhanced mechanical properties. • Suppression of Chemical Reactions: The introduction of SiC nanoparticles effectively suppressed the chemical reactions between FLG and the titanium matrix, preserving the structural integrity of FLG and allowing it to exert its self-lubricating effect. • Improved Mechanical Properties: The tensile strength and tensile modulus of the TMCs increased by 11.74% and 29.35%, respectively, compared to pure TC4, with the addition of SiC accounting for 30 wt% of the FLG content. • Superior Wear Resistance: The wear rate of the TMCs decreased by 52.15% compared to pure TC4, demonstrating a significant improvement in wear resistance. The introduction of graphene endows metals with excellent lubricating properties during friction and wear processes. However, in titanium matrix composites (TMCs), especially during vacuum arc melting with high temperature, intense chemical reactions occur between graphene and Ti, making it difficult to achieve the expected lubricating effect because graphene loses its intact structure. In this study, few-layered graphene (FLG)/SiC/Ti-6Al-4 V (TC4) composite were fabricated using vacuum arc melting methods. Results indicated that the introduction of SiC inhibited the chemical reaction between FLG and the matrix, protecting the structural integrity of FLG and enabling it to exert its self-lubricating effect. After adding SiC accounting for 30 wt% of the FLG content, the tensile strength and the tensile modulus of the TMCs increased by 11.74 % and 29.35 % compared with that of TC4, and the wear rate of the TMCs decreased by 52.15 % compared with that of TC4 and by 49.24 % compared with that of the TMCs without SiC addition. With the increase in SiC content, the wear mode changed, and plastic deformation and adhesive wear gradually disappeared.

llm.why_not_core: Vacuum arc melting is not an additive manufacturing process; this paper does not study additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V.

summary_zh.motivation: 通过真空电弧熔炼制备石墨烯增强Ti-6Al-4V复合材料以提高力学和耐磨性能。
summary_zh.method: 预均化原料后真空电弧熔炼，加入SiC抑制石墨烯与钛的反应。
summary_zh.result: 抗拉强度和模量分别提高11.74%和29.35%，磨损率降低52.15%。

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate graphene-reinforced Ti-6Al-4V composites with enhanced mechanical and wear properties via vacuum arc melting.
summary_en.method: A pre-homogenization and vacuum arc melting method was developed, using SiC nanoparticles to suppress the reaction between graphene and titanium matrix.
summary_en.result: Tensile strength and modulus increased by 11.74% and 29.35%, respectively, and wear rate decreased by 52.15% compared to pure Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing and wear experiments were conducted.
